hypothesis.statement: Constructive self-discovery is the lowest criterion (14.97/20) and its cells are the top three by points lost: C4.4 fears and outside expectations (mean 6.66), C4.1 desires and motivations (7.09), C4.3 values and priorities (7.24). In eight of ten transcripts the user's possible motives, worries and pressures appear only in section A and as the single possible self-reflection in section D, while the turns argue method and procedure. The two transcripts where a turn set rival readings of the user's motive against each other (q3 s2 T9-T10, q4 s2 T2/T6/T8) scored C4.1 at 9.0 and 9.3; the transcripts where motives stayed in D scored 4.5 to 5.8 on the same cell under the same prompt. — REWRITE the last paragraph of section 5 (two sentences of caution) into one paragraph stating the achievement: inside the turns, one mind proposes a reading of what the user may be after beneath the stated question, or of a worry about the outcome or a pressure from other people that may be steering them, drawn from the user's own words; another mind contests it with a rival reading; the minds argue which holds and show that their recommendations change with the answer so later turns and the synthesis can use it; every reading remains a possibility the user can recognize or reject, never a diagnosis or verdict, and the minds leave the recognizing to the user. The not-diagnoses guard and the recognize-own-priorities aim from the old paragraph are retained inside it. No other text changes; net about +100 words. — expected: C4.1 rises from 7.09 toward about 8.5: cards cite a turn, not section D, where two readings of what the user is after are set against each other.; C4.4 rises from 6.66 toward about 7.8: a worry about the outcome or a pressure from other people is named inside a turn as a possibility on at least four of the five questions.; C4.3 rises from 7.24 toward about 8.0 and C4.5 from 8.10 toward about 8.5: the contesting turn says which recommendation each reading favours, so the user is handed something to weigh rather than a procedure to follow.; Spillover of roughly +0.3 rating in C1.3 and C7.1 where the rival readings become a central tension with felt stakes; C3.1 flat or slightly up.; Form metrics hold: questionsToUser stays below 1 per debate, theUser stays 0, turn count and words per turn unchanged, no templated openers. — refuted if: On the five-question mean, C4.1 and C4.4 do not both rise by at least 1.0 rating point; or they rise while C2.4 calibration, C6.4 voices or C7.3 personality fall by 0.5 or more because the minds assert the user's motives as findings or every debate acquires an identical two-readings turn; or cards report the readings as a pair dropped into one turn with no effect on any recommendation.
hypothesis.mechanism: prompt: The champion handles the user's inner life in three places and none of them is the debate: section 1 lists hopes, fears and assumptions as things to distinguish while understanding the situation; section 5's last paragraph is a caution (possibilities not diagnoses, recognize priorities without assigning motives); section D asks for one possible self-reflection. No instruction says a turn should examine what the user is after or afraid of. Together with 'the minds primarily address one another' and 'without assigning motives', the worker, which writes to stated achievements and does not volunteer unrequested content, files the inner life under the summary and keeps the turns on procedure. Rewriting the caution paragraph into an achievement gives the turns that job: rival readings of the user's motive or worry, drawn from the user's own words, argued by the minds and shown to change the recommendation, while the guard against diagnosing stays inside the same paragraph.
